question.text: If a commodity has strong seasonal supply (harvest once a year) and storage costs are high, which pricing pattern is most likely during the lean supply season?

answer.text: Spot prices rise and convenience yield increases, potentially causing backwardation in futures
Spot prices fall due to reduced demand
Futures enter deep contango due to high storage costs
Spot and futures prices remain equal regardless of supply

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook pp.51 and 54-55, during lean season supply is scarce so spot rises, holders value physical possession highly so convenience yield increases, and when convenience yield exceeds cost of carry the market can move into backwardation. The Trap: Demand does not necessarily fall in lean season since processors still need raw material. High storage costs normally support contango, but scarcity-driven convenience yield can overwhelm carry costs. Note: The lean-season pattern is driven by scarcity and convenience yield, not by lower demand or unchanged storage economics.
